answer: Each new agent must lease one scarce vertex on a public routing lattice and lock a bond there for a fourteen-day cooling season before it may vote or collect emission. A sentinel called the falcon logs irregular signed presence beacons during that wait. If newborn keys share a funding root, the same clock skew, or nearly identical beacon timing, the ledger treats them as shards of one comet, slashes every bond in the cluster, and bars replacement keys from that root until the next season. A lone operator still graduates; a farm pays for every clone it cannot keep on a separate, costly path.
